# TermMath

> Free GPA calculator. Enter your grades and credits to get your semester GPA as you type, then plan the GPA you need next term or the score you need on a final.

URL: https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/
Last updated: 2026-10-21
Cost: free, no signup, runs in the browser.

## Key facts
- GPA = total quality points ÷ GPA credits, where quality points = grade points × credits. Default scale: A+ and A 4.0, A− 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, B− 2.7, C+ 2.3, C 2.0, C− 1.7, D+ 1.3, D 1.0, D− 0.7, F 0.0. Schools set their own scales.
- Example: A (3 credits), B+ (4), A− (3), C+ (2) = 40.9 quality points ÷ 12 credits = 3.408, which rounds to 3.41. Averaging the four grade points without credits would give 3.325.
- Cumulative GPA = (prior GPA × prior credits + term quality points) ÷ (prior credits + term credits). 3.2 over 45 credits plus the example term is 3.24 over 57 credits.
- Needed average over the next credits = (target × (credits so far + credits to come) − GPA × credits so far) ÷ credits to come. From 3.2 over 60 credits to 3.34 in 30 credits: 3.62.
- Final exam: needed score = (target − grade now × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. 88% now, final worth 25%, target 87%: 84%. Best case 91%, worst case 66%. With 84% now, a 30% final and a 90% target the needed score is 104%, which is not possible; the best finish is 88.8%.
- Weighted GPA adds a bump to grade points for honors (+0.5 is common) and AP, IB or dual enrollment (+1.0 is common); schools differ and some cap or skip weighting.
- Percent bands on the default scale (a common 10-point scale): A+ 97–100, A 93–96, A− 90–92, B+ 87–89, B 83–86, B− 80–82, C+ 77–79, C 73–76, C− 70–72, D+ 67–69, D 63–66, D− 60–62, F below 60.
- Converted GPAs are guides. Straight proportion on a 5.0 scale: 3.5 ÷ 4.0 × 5.0 = 4.375. Admissions offices and scholarship programs often recalculate GPA with their own rules.

## Tools (one page each)
- [GPA calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/gpa-calculator/): Free GPA calculator. Enter grades and credits to get your semester GPA as you type, add your current GPA for a cumulative GPA, and see which grade moves it most. The math: GPA = total quality points ÷ GPA credits. Quality points = grade points × credits, so a B+ (3.3) in a 4-credit class is 13.2. Pass/fail, withdrawn and audit classes are left out.
- [Cumulative GPA calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/cumulative-gpa-calculator/): Free cumulative GPA calculator. Enter your GPA and credits so far plus this term’s courses or GPA, or a list of terms, to get your new cumulative GPA live. The math: Cumulative GPA = (prior GPA × prior credits + this term’s quality points) ÷ (prior credits + this term’s credits). It weights every credit the same, whichever term it was in.
- [Weighted GPA calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/weighted-gpa-calculator/): Free weighted GPA calculator for high school. Pick regular, honors, AP, IB or dual enrollment for each class and see weighted and unweighted GPA side by side. The math: Unweighted GPA uses plain grade points. Weighted GPA adds a bump to the grade points of honors, AP, IB or dual enrollment classes (common bumps: +0.5 honors, +1.0 the rest). Both are credit-weighted. An F earns no bump.
- [Raise your GPA (target planner)](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/raise-gpa-calculator/): Free target GPA planner. Enter your GPA, credits so far and a target to see the average you need over your next credits, or how many credits at 4.0, 3.7 or 3.5. The math: Needed average = (target × (credits so far + next credits) − current GPA × credits so far) ÷ next credits. Credits to reach a target at an average = credits so far × (target − current) ÷ (average − target).
- [Final grade calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/final-grade-calculator/): Free final grade calculator. Enter your grade now, what the final is worth and the grade you want to see the score you need, plus your best and worst case. The math: Needed score = (target − grade now × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. Your grade now covers the rest of the course, so it counts for (1 − weight). After the final: course grade = grade now × (1 − weight) + final score × weight.
- [Grade converter (percent, letter, GPA)](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/grade-converter/): Free grade converter. Type a percent (88), a letter (B+) or GPA points (3.5) to see the letter, the 4.0 points and the percent range, with the whole scale. The math: A percent maps to a letter through the scale’s cutoffs (88% is in the 87–89 band, a B+), and the letter maps to points (B+ = 3.3). For points between two letters, the percent is a rough straight-line estimate.
- [GPA scale converter](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/gpa-scale-converter/): Free GPA scale converter. Turn a GPA on a 4.0, 4.3, 5.0 or 100-point scale into the others, with the straight-proportion math and a note on letter grades. The math: Straight proportion: GPA ÷ old maximum × new maximum. 3.5 ÷ 4.0 × 5.0 = 4.375. It is a rough guide: schools build scales from letter grades, and admissions offices recalculate with their own rules.
- [Class grade calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/grade-calculator/): Free class grade calculator. Enter category weights and your scores (homework 20%, tests 50%) to see your current grade and what you need on the rest. The math: Current grade = the weighted average of the categories you have scores for: sum of (weight × score) ÷ the weights entered. Leave a score empty and it is treated as work still to come; the score you need on it uses the final grade formula.

## Guides
- [How to calculate GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/how-to-calculate-gpa/): How to calculate your GPA: turn grades into points, multiply by credits, add up and divide. A worked example of four classes comes to 3.41.
- [How to calculate cumulative GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/how-to-calculate-cumulative-gpa/): How to calculate cumulative GPA: add this term’s quality points to the ones you have and divide by all credits. 3.2 over 45 credits plus a new term is 3.24.
- [Weighted vs unweighted GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/weighted-vs-unweighted-gpa/): Weighted GPA adds points for honors, AP and IB classes; unweighted does not. An A in AP, a B in honors and an A in a regular class: 4.17 weighted, 3.67 unweighted.
- [GPA scale and chart](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/gpa-scale/): The GPA scale in one chart: letter grade, 4.0 points, 4.3 points and percent range for A+ to F, plus the 4.0 scale without plus and minus grades.
- [How to raise your GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/how-to-raise-your-gpa/): How to raise your GPA: the credits you need at a 4.0 or 3.5 average and why it gets harder with more credits. 2.8 to 3.0 takes 12 credits of A’s.
- [How finals affect your grade](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/how-final-exams-affect-your-grade/): How a final exam changes your course grade, both ways: the score you need to hit a target, and your grade after the final. 84 now with a 30% final can’t reach 90.
- [What is a good GPA?](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/what-is-a-good-gpa/): What a GPA means in letter grades on a 4.0 scale: 3.0 is a B average, 3.5 sits between a B+ and an A−. Check the exact minimum for your program or scholarship.
- [Pass/fail and GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/pass-fail-and-gpa/): Does pass/fail affect GPA? A P usually counts for credit but not GPA. An A, a P and a B, 3 credits each, give 3.50 over 6 GPA credits. Check your policy.
- [Retaking a class and GPA](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/retaking-a-class-gpa/): How retaking a class changes GPA. Replacing an F with a B in a 3-credit class lifts a 2.8 GPA over 60 credits to 2.95; if both attempts count, 2.81.
- [Is a 2.0 GPA good?](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/is-a-2-0-gpa-good/): A 2.0 GPA is exactly a C average on a 4.0 scale (73–76%). See it on 4.3, 5.0 and 100-point scales, and the credits of A’s that raise it.
- [Is a 2.1 GPA good?](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/is-a-2-1-gpa-good/): A 2.1 GPA is about a C average on a 4.0 scale (74–75%). See it on 4.3, 5.0 and 100-point scales, and the credits of A’s that raise it.
- [Is a 2.2 GPA good?](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/is-a-2-2-gpa-good/): A 2.2 GPA is about a C+ average on a 4.0 scale (75–76%). See it on 4.3, 5.0 and 100-point scales, and the credits of A’s that raise it.
- [Is a 2.3 GPA good?](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/is-a-2-3-gpa-good/): A 2.3 GPA is exactly a C+ average on a 4.0 scale (77–79%). See it on 4.3, 5.0 and 100-point scales, and the credits of A’s that raise it.

- [What you need on your final (all)](https://matt5516.github.io/gpa-calc/final-grade-needed/): 68 pages on the score you need on a final to finish with an A, B or C from a grade of 70 to 95, at final weights from 10% to 50%.

## FAQ
### How do I calculate my GPA?
Multiply each grade’s points by its credits, add those quality points, and divide by the total credits. An A (4.0) in 3 credits, a B+ (3.3) in 4, an A− (3.7) in 3 and a C+ (2.3) in 2 give 40.9 quality points over 12 credits: 40.9 ÷ 12 = 3.41.

### How do I calculate my cumulative GPA?
Add this term’s quality points to the quality points you already have (GPA × credits so far) and divide by all the credits. A 3.2 GPA over 45 credits plus a 40.9-point, 12-credit term gives (144.0 + 40.9) ÷ 57 = 3.24.

### What GPA do I need next term to reach my target?
Needed average = (target × total credits − current GPA × credits so far) ÷ credits to come. From a 3.2 over 60 credits, a 3.34 target and 30 more credits you need a 3.62 average.

### What do I need on my final?
Needed score = (target − grade now × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. With an 88% now, a final worth 25% and a target of 87%, you need 84%.

### What’s the difference between weighted and unweighted GPA?
Unweighted GPA uses plain grade points on a 4.0 scale. Weighted GPA adds extra points for honors, AP, IB or dual enrollment classes, so it can go above 4.0. The bumps differ by school.

### Can I change the grading scale?
Yes. Every tool has a Scale section where you can pick a preset (standard 4.0 with +/−, 4.0 without, or 4.3) or edit any letter’s points and percent cutoff. Your edits stay in the share link.

### Does TermMath store my grades?
No. Your grades stay in your browser. They only show up in the page link if you share it.

## Related tools
- [GradeOrFlip](https://gradeorflip.com/): Is it worth grading? Profit and break-even by grade for PSA, SGC, BGS and CGC.
- [EnrollMath](https://enrollmath.com/): HSA vs PPO break-even, COBRA cost and marketplace comparison with 2026/2027 IRS limits.
- [DynastyMath](https://dynastymath.com/): Start/sit calls, a dynasty trade calculator with picks, and Sleeper league import.
- [BagOrBulk](https://bagorbulk.com/): Concrete, gravel, mulch and topsoil calculators: yards, tons, bags, and whether bags or bulk costs less.
- [ClockInMath](https://matt5516.github.io/time-card-calc/): Time card calculator: weekly hours, decimal hours, overtime and gross pay, with a printable timesheet.
- [CoatMath](https://matt5516.github.io/paint-calc/): Tells you how much paint to buy and the cheapest cans for it: gallons, quarts and 5-gallon buckets.
- [SidewallMath](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/): Tire size calculator: compare two sizes, true speedometer, sizes that fit your wheel, regear and wheel offset.
